text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Road tolls for Bulgarians are expected to be introduced on the country's highways not earlier than October, a senior Road Management Department official said. @

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency had set May 5, 1700 hours local time as the deadline for the Bulgarian-Spanish joint venture Marvex to disburse 10 percent of the $44.5 million it had pledged for acquiring 70 percent of Bulgaria's cement maker Devnya Ziment.

-- Hailstorms can devastate the grain crop in Bulgaria next month because the Agriculture ministry has failed to transfer some 230 million levs for anti-hail missile protection to the National anti-hail service, a senior official said. @
-- Bulgaria's Transport Ministry approved a $63 million financial plan for the modernisation of Bourgas airport on the country's Black Sea coast.

-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) was ready to buy 10 to 12 percent of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC), officials said after a meeting between representatives of the EBRD and BTC.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet is expected to lift controls on fuel prices today and prices were expected to drop by 10 percent on the average from April levels because of the lev rise agains the dollar.

-- Bulgaria would transit Russian natural gas to Turkey over the next 25 years, Bulgargas company director Vassil Filipov said, rejecting media reports that Russia and Turkey had opted for a gas pipeline under the Black Sea instead.
-- Buyers of stakes in Bulgaria's cement plants Granitoid and Zlatna Panega will become known around May 10, Construction ministry officials said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
